newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks come under renewed pressure.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks come under renewed pressure.

text.p: Wall Street stocks came under renewed pressure in early afternoon trading, but no fresh news lay behind the Dow's move to its session lows, traders said.
"It's just more of the same," said Arnie Owen, managing director of capital markets at Cruttenden Roth. "I don't see a preponderance of sellers, just an absence of buyers."
About 1300 EDT/1700 GMT, the Dow fell to a fresh low for the day of 7811.49 before moving to 7830.54, off 111.49, or 1.41 percent.
Earlier the market's move was attributed to the weaker dollar, lower bond prices and jitters over blue-chip earnings.
The long bond was down 13/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
S&P Futures also remained weaker, off 11.55 points at 916.50 points with sidecar curbs imposed.
Sluggish dealings in the European stock markets was also dampening sentiment, helping to make the technology stocks less visible in particular, Owen said.
